title: The Morning Digest: October 19, 2026
dek: Friday's settles stand as the last completed session, Brent Dec26 at $109.86 and WTI Nov26 at $101.41. Overnight both benchmarks eased, Brent to $107.88 and WTI to $100.25 at about 04:27 GMT (Reuters), after the United States waived the Graham Act sanctions and duties on Russia that were due to take effect on Oct 18. The physical board pointed the other way all weekend: Kpler puts Gulf crude flows at about 8.5 Mb/d last week with at least 10 confirmed vessel incidents, Ukraine set fires at the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchi depot in one of its largest drone waves of the war, and the IRGC claimed a third tanker mine strike in Hormuz late Sunday, a claim with no independent confirmation. Riyadh airport reopened on Sunday, was suspended again for several hours the same day, and was gradually resuming, with trackers disagreeing on its exact status this morning. The diesel crack closed Friday at $99.35 on the validated history, a second data point below the $100 regime question that Monday's close now decides. December WCS settled Friday at -$27.40 (ICE TMW settle, Oct 16) on one lot, and the November Mainline apportionment notice, expected today, had not been published as of this edition.
